problem.text:
For real numbers $(x, y, z)$ satisfying the following equations, find all possible values of $x + y + z$.

$x^2y + y^2z + z^2x = -1$

$xy^2 + yz^2 + zx^2 = 5$

$xyz = -2$

steps.title: Where to start: add the first two equations
steps.body: Neither long equation factors by itself. But together they contain all six terms of the form $x^2y$, and the third equation gives $xyz$. Those are exactly the pieces that appear when you expand $(x+y)(y+z)(z+x)$.

steps.title: One pair must add to zero
steps.body: The six terms add to $-1 + 5 = 4$ and $2xyz = -4$, so $(x+y)(y+z)(z+x) = 0$. The system does not change if you rename $x \to y \to z \to x$, so a solution with $y + z = 0$ or $z + x = 0$ can be relabeled into one with $x + y = 0$ and the same sum. So we may take $x = -y$, and then $x + y + z = z$.

your_turn.prompt: Put $x = -y$ into $xyz = -2$. What do you get?

steps.title: Reduce to two variables
steps.body: With $x = -y$, the first equation becomes $y^3 + y^2z - yz^2 = -1$, that is $y(y^2 + yz - z^2) = -1$. The second becomes $-y^3 + yz^2 + y^2z = 5$; using $y^2z = 2$ it turns into $y(z^2 - y^2) = 3$. Careful: if you also replace $y^2z$ by $2$ in the first equation, you get the second one again and learn nothing, so keep the first in its full form.

your_turn.prompt: Divide $y(z^2 - y^2) = 3$ by $y(y^2 + yz - z^2) = -1$ and clear the denominator. Move everything to one side.
your_turn.answer: $z^2 - y^2 = -3(y^2 + yz - z^2)$, so $2y^2 + 3yz - 2z^2 = 0$. (Dividing is safe because the divisor $y(y^2 + yz - z^2)$ equals $-1$, not $0$.)

steps.title: Factor into two cases
steps.body: The quadratic factors as $$2y^2 + 3yz - 2z^2 = (2y - z)(y + 2z) = 0,$$ so either $z = 2y$ or $y = -2z$. In each case, $y^2z = 2$ pins down the numbers.

your_turn.prompt: Check the factorization by expanding $(2y - z)(y + 2z)$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: If $z = 2y$: $2y^3 = 2$, so $y = 1$, $z = 2$, $x = -1$, and the sum is $z = 2$. If $y = -2z$: $4z^3 = 2$, so $z = \sqrt[3]{1/2}$ with $y = -2z$, $x = 2z$, and the sum is $z = \sqrt[3]{1/2}$. Both triples check in all three equations (for example $(-1, 1, 2)$ gives $1 + 2 - 4 = -1$, $-1 + 4 + 2 = 5$ and $-2$). The possible values are **$2$ and $\sqrt[3]{\frac{1}{2}}$**.
